title: Hotline 1.9 protocol documentation gap register
method: Documentation review plus read-only Ghidra MCP follow-up against the recorded Hotline 1.9 data fork, paired resource-fork inspection, portable archive verification, pinned shx source review with seven host callback cases, and mxd review (55 focused tests passed). The original audit and validity ledger remain immutable; current sources have been reviewed and re-snapshotted. No native runtime/client captures or Kani proof results are claimed. Entries remain Investigating while their acceptance criteria are unmet.

gaps.title: Define the supported 1.9 subset

sources.heading: Hotline Server Protocol 1.9: Transactions and Functionality Guide
Open compatibility gaps and QA requirements

gaps.question: Which of the 45 requests and server notifications must mxd implement now, defer explicitly, or reject, and which peer profiles are acceptance targets?
gaps.implementation_impact: An open-ended baseline cannot define feature completion or compatible rejection behaviour.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish an operation-by-profile scope matrix with required, deferred and excluded states, including replies to unsupported operations.

gaps.title: Canonical transaction and field schemas
gaps.question: For every in-scope request, reply and notification, which fields are required, optional, conditional or repeatable, with what widths and value domains?
gaps.implementation_impact: Lists of fields that a handler reads are not sufficient to build a compatible encoder or validator.
gaps.closure_criteria: Provide a schema registry for the core operations, marking each remaining unknown with a gap ID; include direction, cardinality, width, conditions and defaults.

resolution.closure: Published a core operation registry with direction, logical scalar/repeated occurrence, widths/byte caps, default/absence behaviour and conditions. Remaining type, boundary, routing and fixture unknowns retain their separate gap IDs as required by this criterion. This closes the registry deliverable, not all codec/runtime acceptance questions.

gaps.title: Error-code and failure-outcome registry
gaps.question: Which statuses, field-100 forms and connection outcomes apply to each failure, including errors in operations without a normal ACK?
gaps.implementation_impact: Implementations cannot distinguish recoverable failure, success, silent rejection and impending disconnect consistently.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document a failure table and representative bytes for authentication, permission, missing-object, malformed-request and unsupported-operation cases.

resolution.progress: Captured the108-entry native-result table, verified sorted keys and documented representative internal domain/code mappings with resource meanings. These are not wire statuses; enclosing catch translation and native error packets remain required.
resolution.closure: Not closed: remaining acceptance evidence is listed above.

gaps.title: Transaction ID lifecycle and correlation
gaps.question: Are zero, duplicate, wrapped or reused IDs accepted, how are client and server ID spaces separated, and how are unsolicited replies treated?
gaps.implementation_impact: Correlation and reassembly can attach a reply or payload to the wrong outstanding operation.
gaps.closure_criteria: Specify ID allocation, lifetime, wrap/reuse and notification correlation rules; exercise zero, collision and late-reply cases.

resolution.progress: Recorded per-connection increment/zero-skipping wrap and fragment matching. Collision, reuse and late-reply fixtures remain required.
resolution.closure: Not closed: remaining acceptance evidence is listed above.

gaps.title: Connection timers and liveness

sources.heading: Additional Observed Requests and Scope Gaps

gaps.question: What are the handshake, login, agreement, idle and partial-frame deadlines, and what traffic resets them?
gaps.implementation_impact: A client can wait forever or disconnect a compatible session prematurely without a liveness contract.
gaps.closure_criteria: Provide a timer/state table with units, reset conditions, configurable values and close outcomes, distinguishing native observations from mxd limits.

resolution.progress: Published timer origins/reset conditions: only selected logical requests refresh session activity; upload entry clocks begin at request creation and attachment does not reset them; consumed file chunks refresh them. Added bounded pending/partial-input negatives and late-attachment derived case. Lower-layer/configured timing and native boundary fixtures remain required.
resolution.closure: Not closed: remaining acceptance evidence is listed above.
